This Appeal Coming On For Admssion, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.1349/2012, vide judgment and award dated 13.02.2017.
2.

sentences.text: The claimant suffered injuries, when he was getting down from a bus belonging to North-East Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (NEKRTC) (henceforth referred as 'Corporation) on 28.04.2012.

The claimant suffered fracture of left foot and was shifted to Kamareddy Hospital,
Kalaburagi.
The claimant claimed that he was 45 years old and was an agriculturist earning a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month.
He claimed that due to the injuries, he was not in a position to earn his livelihood NC: 2023:KHC-K:1245 and
hence sought for compensation from the owner and insurer of the bus.
3. The claim petition was contested by the insurer, who denied the accident and also claimed that the driver of the bus was not negligent.
The Corporation admitted the accident but claimed that the accident was not due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P12.
He examined a doctor as PW.2, who deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 40% to the lower limb and 15% to 20% to the whole body.
The Tribunal considered the evidence on record and held that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus.
It noted that the claimant was treated as an inpatient from 28.04.2012 to 03.05.2012 during which time, he underwent a surgery for fixing the fracture.

It also noticed that the claimant had suffered fracture of NC: 2023:KHC-K:1245 fibula and fracture of lower third of left fibula and x-ray report indicated a malunited fracture of lower third shaft of left fibula.

It considered the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.4,500/- per month and determined the disability suffered by the claimant at 8% to the whole body and awarded the following compensation:

Pain and suffering Rs.25,000/-

Medical Expenses Rs.5,000/-
Attendant & conveyance Rs.1,000 charges Loss of future income Rs.87,696/-
The Tribunal directed the insurer of the bus to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded, the claimant is in appeal.

The learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that the claimant had suffered fracture of lower third shaft of left fibula and therefore, it was impossible for him to engage in any agricultural activity.
He submitted that while calculating the disability, the Tribunal must have assessed functional disability rather than physical disability.

He submitted that as against the evidence of PW.2 that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 40% to the lower limb and 15% to 20% to the whole body, the Tribunal had wrongly considered the same at 8%.

He submitted that this Court in similar circumstances has considered the notional income at a sum of Rs.6,500/-
per month.
He also contended that the Tribunal failed to award compensation towards loss of amenities and loss of income during the period of treatment and also towards future medical expenses.

7. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent/insurer supported the impugned judgment and award and contended that the fractures were united and NC: 2023:KHC-K:1245 the claimant did not suffer any major disability and he could still work as a labour.
8. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant as well as the learned counsel for the respondent/insurer.
9. The accident in question is not in dispute.
It is also not in dispute that the claimant had suffered injuries in the accident.
The records disclose that the claimant had suffered fracture of lower third shaft of left fibula and other injuries.
It is also not in dispute that the claimant was admitted in the hospital as an inpatient on 28.04.2012 and was discharged on 03.05.2012.

The claimant claimed to be an agriculturist and therefore, the injuries must have caused some amount of disability having regard to the nature of work that the claimant used to do to earn his livelihood.
Therefore, it is appropriate to consider the disability suffered by the claimant at 10% to the whole body.
As rightly contended by the learned counsel for appellant/claimant, this Court had considered the notional Shankar vs S.K.Akbar And Ors on 19 June, 2023

There is no reason why the claimant should not be extended the same benefit.
Further, the Tribunal failed to award any compensation towards loss of amenities, loss of income during the period of treatment as well as towards future medical expenses.

Therefore,
considering the above, the compensation to which the claimant is entitled to is re- determined as follows:
Pain and suffering Rs.25,000/-
Medical Expenses Rs.5,000/-
Attendant & conveyance Rs.5,000/-
charges Loss of future income Rs.1,09,200/-
(Rs.6,500x12x14x10%)
Loss of income during the Rs.19,500/-
period of treatment (Rs.6,500x3)
Loss of amenities Rs.40,000/-
Future medical expenses Rs.10,000/-
Total Rs.2,13,700/-
 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1245 10.

In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the compensation of Rs.1,18,700/-
determined by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.2,13,700/-.
The enhanced compensation of Rs.95,000/- shall be paid by the insurer to the claimant along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment and award.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years.
